checks.reason: For every boundary point and neighbourhood there is a compact cornered domain, one continuous frame quadruple and epsilon>0, such that every epsilon-close continuous quadruple has an unbounded absolute value of the signed curvature integral along a sequence which may depend on that quadruple. The absolute value is outside the integral. The additional angular-shift L1 hypothesis and Proposition3.6 assumptions are retained. The conclusion concerns the specified affinely parametrized future-inextendible timelike geodesic endpoints, not all extension problems or global cosmic censorship.

checks.source_locations: Full current report; coverage entries C2-C8 and source Theorem3.14
checks.reason: The report describes logarithmic energy control using finite coordinate changes and the L1 coefficient, the two-sided ODE estimate, connecting curves with varying v over shrinking intervals, fixed smoothed test fields and bounded Stokes terms. External identification propositions remain explicit dependencies, not newly proved results. The universal perturbation condition is needed to permit the fixed smoothed quadruple; no L1 absolute-curvature bound is substituted.

Direct differentiation gives r'=-cos(-1/v), r''=sin(-1/v)/v^2. Retaining the volume factor r^2, integration by parts bounds the unperturbed signed integral. After the stated weighted perturbation, the extra term becomes -integral r(-1/x)^2 sin^2(x)/x dx and diverges; a cutoff perturbation can remove that divergence. The report correctly treats this as failure of a weaker robustness hypothesis rather than a counterexample to Theorem3.14.
